entries.clue: Football association secures revolutionary tie (6)

indicatorNotes.revolutionary: a revolution turns something round, so the word it describes is read backwards

annotation.surface: A football governing body clinches a thrilling, game-changing match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Secures' looks like a container instruction wrapping 'tie'; it is really the verb NETS, and 'tie' is the definition sitting at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: tying a knot or a lace secures it in place.

entries.clue: Joined around old college as directed (7)

indicatorNotes.around: one piece goes around the other

annotation.surface: Someone joined up with an old college, as they were instructed to.
annotation.walkthrough: FUSED goes around O and C, giving F(OC)USED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: attention aimed at one target has been concentrated there.

entries.clue: Brown pea is pulped (5)

indicatorNotes.pulped: pulping mashes something into a new shape

annotation.surface: A brown pea has been mashed to mush.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brown' reads as a colour describing the pea; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown colour, the tint of old photographs.

entries.clue: Old dogs I directed towards Sally (9)

blocks.note: on = directed towards, as in 'turned on'

annotation.surface: Someone sends their old dogs off towards a woman called Sally.
annotation.walkthrough: Sally looks like a woman's name; with a lower-case sense, a sally is an outing or trip.
annotation.definitionFit: A less common sense of sally: besides a military sortie, it is a brief trip or outing.

entries.clue: Dig dome out for Maui perhaps (7)

indicatorNotes.out: out = not in its usual order

annotation.surface: An instruction to excavate a dome, perhaps on the Hawaiian island of Maui.
annotation.walkthrough: Maui looks like the Hawaiian island; it is also the demigod of Polynesian myth, and 'perhaps' flags him as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Maui is a demigod in Polynesian mythology, famous for fishing up islands.

entries.clue: Stand up unusual cleaning aid (7)

indicatorNotes.unusual: the letters are in an unusual order

annotation.surface: A household gadget that stands upright, which is unusual for it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stand up' reads as an instruction or as describing the aid; it is only letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A dustpan is used with a brush to clean up.

entries.clue: Masculine coat hung outside at first (5)

indicatorNotes.at first: take the first letter of each word it follows

blocks.note: a mac is a raincoat (short for mackintosh)

annotation.surface: A man's coat has been hung up outside to begin with.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outside' looks like a container instruction; here it only supplies its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: the word, from Spanish for 'male', describes showily manly behaviour.

entries.clue: Dug soil up around LA to produce bloom (9)

indicatorNotes.up: dug up soil is churned, so its letters are mixed
indicatorNotes.around: LA joins the mix of letters around it

blocks.note: LA as printed, joins the fodder

annotation.surface: A gardener in Los Angeles turns over the soil to grow flowers.
annotation.walkthrough: LA reads as Los Angeles; it is just two more letters for the mix.
annotation.definitionFit: The gladiolus is a tall garden flower, so a bloom.

entries.clue: Machine for deepening harbour deserted by river side (6)

annotation.surface: A dredging machine sits idle, abandoned on the riverbank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deserted by' looks like a deletion instruction; 'deserted' is only D and 'by' puts the pieces side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: A dredge is a machine that scoops mud from the bottom to deepen a harbour.

entries.clue: Setter taking test showing degree of optimism (6)

indicatorNotes.taking: one piece takes in the other

blocks.note: the setter refers to themselves as ME, the outer piece
an oral is a spoken test

annotation.surface: The crossword setter sits an exam and reveals how hopeful they feel.
annotation.walkthrough: ME takes in ORAL: M(ORAL)E.
annotation.definitionFit: Morale is the level of confidence and optimism in a person or group.

entries.clue: Big top a circus initially promises (9)

indicatorNotes.initially: 'initially' means at the start, so only the start of 'circus' is used

blocks.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle
IOUs are written promises to pay

annotation.surface: A circus advertises its huge tent, the big top.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Big top' is a circus tent, so the surface glues the two words together; they split, with 'Big' the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Capacious means roomy, able to hold a lot, so big.

entries.clue: Box in clubs with speed (5)

annotation.surface: A boxer fights, with fists or clubs, as fast as they can.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Box in' looks like an instruction to put something inside; 'Box' is the definition and 'in' merely links.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a slatted wooden container used to ship goods.

entries.clue: Knight accepting thanks for one in flight (5)

indicatorNotes.accepting: the outer piece accepts, takes in, the other

blocks.note: a knight is addressed as Sir, the outer piece

annotation.surface: A knight gratefully takes a thank-you from a passenger on a plane.
annotation.walkthrough: SIR accepts TA: S(TA)IR. 'Flight' suggests air travel; a flight is also a run of stairs.
annotation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is made of single stairs, each one in the flight.

entries.clue: Admiring programme with roaming (9)

blocks.note: an app is a computer program

annotation.surface: Someone likes a phone plan that includes roaming abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Approving means looking on something favourably, admiring it.

entries.clue: Lessening recession (7)

blocks.note: a noun: a falling-off in amount or strength
a noun: a downturn, or a moving back

annotation.surface: An economic report notes a shrinking economy.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words read as one phrase about the economy; each on its own means the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A decline is both a lessening and a falling back, a recession.

entries.clue: Barrel maker and wastrel regularly work together (9)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals, every second one

annotation.surface: A barrel maker and a lazy good-for-nothing team up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And' just joins the pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word is built from Latin 'co-' (together) and 'operari' (to work).

entries.clue: Lay net out tidily (6)

indicatorNotes.out: laid out, spread into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A fisherman is told to spread the net out neatly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lay net out' reads as one instruction; 'out' is the anagram signal and 'tidily' the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain adverb synonym: done in an orderly, well-kept way.

entries.clue: Correction of last word on private message by hospital department (9)

blocks.note: amen is the last word of a prayer
DM = direct message, sent privately on social media

annotation.surface: Someone corrects the final word of a private message sent by a hospital department.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' and 'by' only place the pieces in order.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a change made to fix or improve a text, as to a law.

entries.clue: Hard growth on head alien bug (6)

blocks.note: a horn grows from an animal's head

annotation.surface: An alien bug has a hard bump on its head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bug' is the definition in the loose everyday sense of insect.
annotation.definitionFit: A hornet is a large wasp, loosely a bug.

entries.clue: Cheater upset rabbi? (7)

indicatorNotes.upset: upsetting knocks the letters out of order

annotation.surface: A rabbi is dismayed to discover a cheat.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a rabbi is one example of a teacher; the word itself means 'my master' or teacher.
annotation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish teacher of religious law.

entries.clue: Exercise before cat returns (5-2)

indicatorNotes.returns: the word goes back the way it came

annotation.surface: Someone does their workout before the cat comes back home.
annotation.walkthrough: A press-up is the British name for a push-up.
annotation.definitionFit: A press-up is a floor exercise pushing the body up with the arms.

entries.clue: Piano with a canvas covering is conspicuous (6)

blocks.note: a tent is a canvas shelter

annotation.surface: A piano draped under a canvas sheet stands out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covering' looks like a container instruction; here 'canvas covering' is just TENT.
annotation.definitionFit: Patent (as in 'patent nonsense') means obvious, plainly conspicuous.

entries.clue: Melody to pinch revolting seed (4,3)

indicatorNotes.revolting: revolting = turning over, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A song about stealing a disgusting seed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' pretends to mean disgusting, but it turns the whole joined string over, not just the word next to it.
annotation.definitionFit: A botanical fact: the 'nut' is really the edible seed from a pine cone.

entries.clue: French fish with heart removed is toxic (6)

annotation.definitionNote: POISON is a noun; 'toxic' is an adjective, loosely matched as in 'poison gas'

indicatorNotes.with heart removed: the middle letter is taken out

blocks.note: the middle S of POISSON goes

annotation.surface: A French chef guts a fish because its insides are poisonous.
annotation.walkthrough: POISSON has seven letters, so its heart is the fourth, an S.
annotation.definitionFit: Poison is a toxic substance, and used before a noun it means toxic.

entries.clue: Six deliveries by doctor behind bank arrangement (9)

blocks.note: in cricket an over is six balls bowled
aft = behind, at the back of a ship

annotation.surface: A doctor takes delivery of six parcels and falls behind with the bank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests the post; in cricket a delivery is a bowled ball, and six make an over.
annotation.definitionFit: An overdraft is an arrangement letting you borrow from the bank beyond your balance.

entries.clue: Headed back to hot island somewhere in India (5)

indicatorNotes.back: the word before it goes backwards

annotation.surface: A traveller heads back to a hot island somewhere in India.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To' just joins the pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by place: the capital territory in the north of India qualifies as somewhere there.

entries.clue: Clamour about V&A furniture item (5)

indicatorNotes.about: one piece goes about the other

annotation.surface: A public outcry over a piece of furniture at the V&A.
annotation.walkthrough: The V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London, strong on furniture; here it only gives VA. DIN goes about it: DI(VA)N.
annotation.definitionFit: A divan is a low couch or bed.

entries.clue: View six tailless deer (5)

indicatorNotes.tailless: the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: STAG with its last letter gone

annotation.surface: A scene of six deer that have lost their tails.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' reads as describing the animals; it trims the last letter of STAG.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from Italian for 'sight', usually a long, framed outlook.

entries.clue: Marshal leading section for will (5)

indicatorNotes.section: a section of the words is the answer

annotation.surface: A marshal heads the part of a parade put on for a will.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between 'Marshal' and 'leading'.
annotation.definitionFit: Shall and will both form the future tense.

entries.clue: Husband annoys working dependants (7-2)

blocks.note: on = working, as a switched-on machine

annotation.surface: A husband is irritated by the family members who live off him while he works.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Working' looks like it describes the dependants; it is ON.
annotation.definitionFit: Hangers-on are people who depend on another for support or favour.

entries.clue: More attention-seeking wild reindeer losing head (7)

indicatorNotes.wild: wild letters run in no fixed order

annotation.surface: A wild reindeer craves more attention after losing its head.
annotation.walkthrough: The R goes first, then the remaining seven letters are rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone needier demands more attention and support.

entries.clue: Narrow passage artist represented (6)

indicatorNotes.represented: re-presented, the letters shown again in a new order

annotation.surface: An artist has painted a narrow passageway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Represented' sounds like the artist's work; it tells you to rearrange ARTIST.
annotation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow stretch of water between two seas.
